We have many clues. Molecular formula C8H15NO. DBE =2. Aromatic carbons count =2, so there is an aromatic ring? But only 2 aromatic carbons suggests maybe a phenyl? But phenyl has 6 aromatic carbons. 2 aromatic carbons could be part of a heteroaromatic? But formula C8 suggests small. Aromatic carbons 2 suggests maybe a double bond? Actually aromatic carbons count maybe from NMR: 2 aromatic carbons signals. Could be a carbonyl attached to aromatic? But only 2 aromatic carbons suggests maybe a heterocycle like pyridine? But N present already. But formula C8H15NO: one N, one O. DBE 2: could be one ring + one double bond, or two double bonds, etc. Aromatic carbons 2 suggests maybe a double bond (alkene) counted as aromatic? Not likely. Could be a carbonyl (C=O) counts as DBE 1. Another DBE maybe a ring. So maybe a cyclic amide? But aromatic carbons 2 maybe from a carbonyl attached to a phenyl? But phenyl would be 6 aromatic carbons.

Given fragments: 'C(=O)N' (amide), 'C(C)(C)C' (tert-butyl), 'C(C)C' (isopropyl). Combine? Possibly overall SMILES: CC(C)C(=O)NC(C)(C)C? Let's count atoms: CC(C)C = isobutyl? Actually CC(C)C is isobutyl? Let's parse: C C (C) C: that's 4 carbons. Then ( =O)N attached to that carbonyl carbon. Then NC(C)(C)C is tert-butyl attached to N. So total carbons: the carbonyl carbon is one, plus the CC(C)C fragment (4), plus the tert-butyl (4) but note carbonyl carbon counted already? Actually fragments: C(=O)N is carbonyl carbon + O + N. C(C)(C)C is a carbon attached to three methyls (tert-butyl central carbon). That's 4 carbons. C(C)C is isopropyl? That's 3 carbons. Sum: carbonyl carbon (1) + isopropyl (3) + tert-butyl (4) = 8 carbons. Good. Hydrogens: isopropyl: CH (attached to carbonyl) has 1 H, plus two CH3 (6 H) =7. Tert-butyl attached to N: central carbon quaternary (no H), three CH3 (9 H). Total H =7+9=16? plus maybe carbonyl carbon none. So total H 16. But formula says H15. So maybe one less H due to N attached to carbonyl and tert-butyl, N has H? In SMILES above, N is attached to carbonyl carbon and to tert-butyl carbon, and also has H? In SMILES "C(=O)N" then "NC(C)(C)C" means N attached to carbonyl and to tert-butyl carbon, and also has H (since not fully substituted). So N has one H, adding one H. Wait we counted H on N? In our count we didn't include N-H. So total H =16+1 =17? Actually we need recalc: isopropyl side: carbonyl carbon attached to isopropyl carbon (CH). That CH has one H. Two methyls each 3 H =6. So isopropyl side gives 7 H. Tert-butyl side: central carbon attached to N and three methyls. Methyls 9 H. Central carbon no H. N has one H. So total H =7+9+1 =17. That's too many. But formula C8H15NO. So our candidate has too many H. Maybe the isopropyl is actually a carbonyl attached to isopropyl? Wait fragments: C(C)C maybe is just a carbon attached to two methyls (i.e., isopropyl carbon) but that carbon is the carbonyl carbon? Actually fragment list: 'C(=O)N', 'C(C)(C)C', 'C(C)C'. They are fragments to link. Could be carbonyl carbon attached to C(C)C (isopropyl) and N attached to C(C)(C)C (tert-butyl). So SMILES: CC(C)C(=O)N C(C)(C)C? That is same as earlier but order reversed. That gave 17 H. Something off.

Maybe the N is tertiary (no H). Then formula would be C8H16NO? Actually if N has no H, H count 16. Still off. Need H15. So maybe one of the methyl groups is missing? But fragments fixed.
